The '''1921 German football championship''', the 14th edition of the competition, was won by [[1. FC Nürnberg]], defeating [[SpVgg Blau-Weiß 1890 Berlin|BFC Vorwärts 90]] 5–0 in the final.<ref name="Rsssf" >{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duithistpre45.html |title=German championship 1921 |website= Rsssf.com |access-date= 8 January 2016}}</ref>

For 1. FC Nürnberg it was the second national championship, having won the competition in the previous season as well. Nuremberg thereby became the first team to successfully defend their title. It was part of Nuremberg's most successful era where the club won five titles in eight seasons from 1920 to 1927, missing out on a sixth one in the inconclusive 1922 championship. For Vorwärts Berlin it marked the club's sole German championship final. The club, being unrelated to the [[East German]] club [[ASK Vorwärts Berlin]], later merged with 1905 champions [[Union 92 Berlin]] to form [[SpVgg Blau-Weiß 1890 Berlin]].<ref name="List" >{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duitchamp.html |title=(West) Germany -List of champions |website= Rsssf.com |access-date= 8 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/teams/1-fc-nuernberg/1/ |title= 1. FC Nürnberg » Steckbrief |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 8 January 2016|language=de|trans-title= 1. FC Nürnberg honours}}</ref>

Nuremberg's [[Luitpold Popp]] was the top scorer of the 1921 championship with five goals.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/torschuetzenkoenige/deutsche-meisterschaft/ |title=Deutsche Meisterschaft » Torschützenkönige |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 8 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=German championship: Top goal scorer}}</ref>

Seven clubs qualified for the knock-out competition, nominally the champions of each of the seven regional football championships. However, the Baltic championship was later awarded to a different club, the [[VfB Königsberg]].<ref name="Rsssf" />
